title: The 5-Level Agent Ladder: From Booth Helper to Dispatch Hub
summary: Build confidence one step at a time—starting with a 5-minute shift formatter before connecting live Excel trackers and Teams dispatch alerts.

intro.what: A five-stage roadmap tailored for Parking & Transportation teams so anyone can start small and grow at their own pace.
intro.features: Levels 1–3 take 5 to 20 minutes in Agent Builder with zero code. Levels 4–5 add guided permit intake and automated dispatch alerts in Copilot Studio.
intro.exchange: Start with read-only appeal and permit reply drafters before automating notifications.
intro.m365: Level 3 (Live SharePoint Folder Agent) handles 80% of daily booth, enforcement, and event-planning lookups.
intro.developer: Progression: Prompt Formatting -> Single Handbook Q&A -> Live SharePoint Folder -> Guided Intake & Excel Logging -> Triggered Multi-Agent Dispatch.
sources: Microsoft · Choose between Agent Builder and Copilot Studio

sections.title: How Each Rung Helps Your Operation
paragraphs: Level 1 — Shift & Radio Formatter (5 min): No files needed. Turns messy gate, meter, or shuttle notes into clean shift handoff summaries.
Level 2 — Rulebook Q&A & Quiz Coach (10 min): Attaches Parking-Transit-Handbook.txt to answer permit, shuttle, and appeal rules with Rule IDs—or quiz new hires.
Level 3 — Live SharePoint Folder & CSV Auditor (20 min): Links a live SharePoint folder of detour maps and rates, and audits CSV logs for open gate repairs or event overflow.
Level 4 — Guided Permit & Charter Bus Intake (Copilot Studio): Asks event coordinators step-by-step questions, checks Lot D / Bus Apron rules, shows a confirmation card, and logs rows to Excel.
Level 5 — Triggered Dispatch & Multi-Agent Router (Copilot Studio): Alerts supervisors when large events (>40 vehicles) or ADA lift outages occur, and routes questions across specialist agents.

title: Grounding & The Knowledge Fence: Zero Guessing on Fees or Tows
summary: Keep your agent fenced inside approved policy files so it never invents fine amounts, grace periods, or shuttle times.

intro.what: Grounding forces the agent to check your approved Parking & Transit files before answering.
intro.features: Turning Web Search OFF and requiring Rule ID citations stops hallucinations cold.
intro.exchange: Ensure customer appeal emails quote exact 14-day deadlines [Rule AP-01] rather than vague estimates.
intro.m365: Keep active SOPs in a clean SharePoint folder ('Parking-Approved-SOPs') and move expired semester maps to an Archive folder outside the agent's scope.
intro.developer: Grounding honors SharePoint permissions per user at query time.
sources: Microsoft · Knowledge sources in Agent Builder

sections.title: Three Rules That Keep Policy Answers Safe
paragraphs: In parking and transit operations, a wrong guess causes angry drivers at the gate or missed ADA pickups. Always include these three rules in your Instructions: (1) 'Answer ONLY from the attached Knowledge files.' (2) 'Put the exact Rule ID in brackets after every claim.' (3) 'If a rule is not in the file, say: Not covered in our handbook—check with Parking Dispatch.'
Also keep your SharePoint folder tidy: put one current file per topic (Rates, Shuttles, Appeals, Event Overflow) and remove old drafts so the agent never quotes last year's permit price.
sources: Microsoft · Write effective instructions for declarative agents
